instructions: Halve the potatoes and put them in a pot with cold water to cover and 1 tsp of the salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.

Meanwhile, pat the chops dry and season both sides with the remaining 1 tsp of salt and the pepper. Finely chop the shallots, mince the garlic, mince the cornichons to about 3 tbsp, and chop 2 tbsp of parsley.
Heat the oil and 1 tbsp of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat until the butter foams. Add the chops and cook for 4 minutes, until the underside is deep brown and lets go of the pan.

Flip the chops, turn the heat to medium-low and cover the pan. Cook for 5 minutes. You're cooking the pork to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest chop: it should be just barely pink in the middle and the juices clear.
Transfer the chops to a plate and cover them loosely with foil.
Add the shallots to the same pan over medium heat and cook for 1 minute. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds. Add the wine and scrape up the browned bits.
Add the broth and any juices from the plate. Bubble for 3 minutes, until the sauce is reduced by about half.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the mustard, the cornichons and 1 tbsp of the butter until the butter melts.
Drain the potatoes and return them to the pot. Add the last 1 tbsp of butter and toss until it melts.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Spoon the sauce over the chops and sprinkle with the parsley. Serve with the buttered potatoes.
method_notes: No version of this dish had 20 or more ratings (the Food.com page and the Reluctant Gourmet sauce page show none), so the lead is the Food.com pork chops with mustard and cornichon sauce, the closest real version of the whole dish. It sears the chops, keeps the pan, and stirs mustard and minced cornichons in off the heat. The Reluctant Gourmet charcutiere sauce adds shallot, white wine and a reduced stock base, so I used wine and chicken broth in place of Food.com's water. Saveur's version could not be read (403).
